people.peter.role: Simon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ
people.peter.relations: He writes to believers who share his precious faith. He calls Paul our beloved brother.
people.peter.meaning: He says he will keep reminding the readers, because his death is near. He says he and others heard the voice from heaven on the holy mountain. He warns of false teachers and mockers. He ends by telling the readers to grow in grace and knowledge.
people.jesus.role: Lord and Savior, whose coming is promised
people.jesus.relations: Peter says the voice from the Majestic Glory called him “my beloved Son.”
people.jesus.meaning: Peter says God’s power gives all things for life and godliness through knowing him. On the holy mountain, Peter heard the Father’s voice honor him. Mockers ask where the promise of his coming is. Peter tells the readers to be patient. They should keep growing in grace and knowledge of him.
people.noah.role: Preacher of righteousness, kept safe in the flood
people.noah.relations: God kept him with seven others when the flood came.
people.noah.meaning: Peter says God did not spare the ancient world. He kept Noah with seven others when the flood came. Noah is one of Peter’s proofs that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly.
people.lot.relations: Peter names him with the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.
people.lot.meaning: Peter says Lot lived among the wicked. Their lawless deeds tormented him day by day. God delivered him. Sodom and Gomorrah were turned to ashes. Peter says the Lord knows how to deliver the godly.
people.balaam.role: Son of Beor, a prophet who loved wages
people.balaam.relations: He is called the son of Beor. Peter says the false teachers followed his way.
people.balaam.meaning: Peter says Balaam loved the wages of wrongdoing. He was rebuked for his disobedience. A speechless donkey spoke with a man’s voice and stopped his madness. Peter says the false teachers left the right way as he did.
people.paul.role: Our beloved brother, who wrote letters
people.paul.relations: Peter calls him our beloved brother. Peter says Paul wrote to these readers.
people.paul.meaning: Peter says Paul wrote to the readers about the Lord’s patience. Peter says some things in Paul’s letters are hard to understand. The ignorant and unsettled twist them, as they twist the other Scriptures.
places.sodom.summary: Peter recalls Sodom and Gomorrah in chapter 2. God turned the cities to ashes as an example. He delivered righteous Lot from there.
places.sodom.limits: The site is disputed. The marker shows a region, not a confirmed city.
sources.web.summary: The full text of Second Peter is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: Peter is the named speaker. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, and the audience’s situation were not checked independently. The holy mountain’s identity was not checked either. The text gives no calculated date for the coming day. Sodom is only a marker for a disputed region.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-48.summary: The lesson links growth in Christlike qualities to sharing in the divine nature.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-48.limits: Only the lesson’s talk about Second Peter chapter 1 supports this reference. First Peter ideas, linked talks, and Restoration texts do not extend it to other chapters.
sources.lange-peter.summary: Lange reads waiting as hope that changes how people live now.
sources.lange-peter.limits: This is Lange’s own reading. His claim about the author was not checked independently. His Greek comparisons and wider historical claims were not checked either. The text gives no date for the promised coming.
sources.atlas.summary: This atlas from the Church shows the wider setting and marks some disputed places.
sources.atlas.limits: Treat the place labels as background. The linked atlas also has Latter-day Saint commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This atlas from the Church shows towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: The coordinates are estimates for display. A town marker does not prove each event in the text.
chapters.*.mapNote: The Sodom marker shows a disputed region, not a confirmed city.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: Second Peter names no travel route, so the map draws none.
